title: Division operator / without DIVIDE — no BLANK/error handling
description: The / operator raises an error (or returns infinity) when the denominator is 0 and does not handle BLANK. DIVIDE returns BLANK (or an alternate result) instead. Not flagged: a constant non-zero denominator ([Sales] / 1000, / (60*60*24), / POWER(10, 6)) and a denominator the enclosing CALCULATE / FILTER already excludes zero from (canon rule 4 exception 2). Inside an iterator the finding is info: DIVIDE is a per-row callback, so keep / only if zero is provably impossible. Import-mode advice: in DirectQuery DIVIDE does not fold to SQL, so check the storage mode first (exception 3).

title: SWITCH without default/else value
description: SWITCH without a default value returns BLANK when no condition matches. This is often unintentional and can cause confusing report behavior.
fix_suggestion: Add a default value as the last argument to SWITCH, e.g., SWITCH(expr, val1, res1, val2, res2, defaultResult)

title: Potential BLANK propagation in arithmetic
description: `1 - DIVIDE(a, b)` / `1 - a / b` returns 1 when the ratio is BLANK (b is 0 or BLANK), so rows that should be empty show 100 %.

match.description: A numeric literal immediately followed by '-' and a DIVIDE(...) call or an a / b ratio

fix_suggestion: VAR _ratio = DIVIDE(a, b) RETURN IF(NOT ISBLANK(_ratio), 1 - _ratio)

title: IFERROR forces step-by-step evaluation
description: IFERROR must evaluate the expression first and then check for errors, preventing the engine from optimizing the execution plan. Use DIVIDE for division errors, or handle edge cases explicitly. Import-mode advice: in DirectQuery IFERROR folds into the generated SQL and DIVIDE does not, so check the table's storage mode before replacing it (canon rule 4 exception 3 / AP-06).
fix_suggestion: Replace with DIVIDE for division errors, or use IF with explicit condition checks

title: ISERROR forces step-by-step evaluation
description: ISERROR evaluates the full expression to check for errors, preventing query optimization. Handle specific error conditions explicitly instead. Import-mode advice: in DirectQuery IFERROR folds into the generated SQL and DIVIDE does not, so check the table's storage mode before replacing it (canon rule 4 exception 3 / AP-06).
fix_suggestion: Check for the specific condition that causes the error (e.g., division by zero, missing relationship) instead of catching all errors

title: SUMMARIZE with inline expressions — use ADDCOLUMNS+SUMMARIZE or SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
description: SUMMARIZE with more than 2 arguments likely contains inline aggregation expressions. This deprecated pattern can produce incorrect results when the aggregation references columns not in the groupBy set.
fix_suggestion: Use ADDCOLUMNS(SUMMARIZE(table, groupByCol), "Name", expression) or SUMMARIZECOLUMNS

title: INTERSECT — consider TREATAS for virtual relationships
description: INTERSECT materializes both tables. When used for filtering, TREATAS creates a virtual relationship without materialization, which is more efficient and clearer in intent.
fix_suggestion: If used for filtering, replace with TREATAS(VALUES(col), targetTable[col])

title: Hardcoded date literal in CALCULATE
description: A hard-coded date literal in a CALCULATE filter (Date[Year] = 2024, Date[Date] >= DATE(2024,1,1)) goes stale when the data moves on. Literal predicates on non-date columns (a country, an amount threshold, a fixed currency) are normal and are not flagged.

match.description: CALCULATE with a hard-coded date / year literal in a filter

fix_suggestion: Use a slicer, a relative date expression (MAX(Date[Date]), TODAY()) or a disconnected parameter table for the period.
